team_games.selectStr:
WITH sides AS (
    SELECT Id AS game_id, Season AS season, "Week" AS week_number, SeasonType AS season_type,
      StartDate AS start_date, Completed AS completed, ConferenceGame AS conference_game,
      TRUE AS is_home, HomeTeam AS team, HomeConference AS conference, HomeClassification AS classification,
      AwayTeam AS opponent, AwayConference AS opponent_conference, AwayClassification AS opponent_classification,
      HomePoints AS points_for, AwayPoints AS points_against,
      HomePregameElo AS pregame_elo, HomePostgameElo AS postgame_elo, AwayPregameElo AS opponent_pregame_elo
    FROM cfb_games
    UNION ALL
    SELECT Id, Season, "Week", SeasonType,
      StartDate, Completed, ConferenceGame,
      FALSE, AwayTeam, AwayConference, AwayClassification,
      HomeTeam, HomeConference, HomeClassification,
      AwayPoints, HomePoints,
      AwayPregameElo, AwayPostgameElo, HomePregameElo
    FROM cfb_games
  )
  SELECT *,
    CAST(game_id AS VARCHAR) || '|' || team AS team_game_id,
    -- the team's most recent game that carries a postgame Elo, so a
    -- ranking can show where the rating stands now
    postgame_elo IS NOT NULL
      AND row_number() OVER (
        PARTITION BY team, season, postgame_elo IS NULL ORDER BY start_date DESC
      ) = 1 AS is_latest_rated_game
  FROM sides

#|(doc)
One row per team per game in the 2025 and 2026 seasons: every game appears twice, once
from each team's side, with points for and against, the team's and opponent's conference
and division, and pregame and postgame Elo. Joins the drives the team ran and the drives it
defended, so a team's record, scoring margin and drive efficiency on both sides of the ball
come from one source. Use it for team rankings, records and strength of schedule.

fields.name: is_overtime_conversion
fields.code: StartPeriod >= 5 and DriveResult = 'Uncategorized' and Plays <= 1 and Yards = 0

notes.text:
#|(doc)
True when this possession is an overtime two-point conversion attempt rather than a
drive. From the third overtime on, the rules stop giving each team a possession from
the opponent's 25 and give it a single snap from the 3 instead, alternating until one
team converts and the other does not.

The feed has no name for these. It files all nine of them under the literal result
string "Uncategorized", every one a single play that gains nothing — and that pair of
facts, inside overtime, identifies them exactly. Period alone will not do it: the
feed skips a period in Missouri-Auburn and labels an ordinary 7-play touchdown drive
as the seventh period.

#(doc) True when an overtime two-point conversion attempt was good. Read from the feed's Scoring flag, which tracks these correctly — it reproduces the 53-51 finish of the nine-period South Dakota game exactly.

fields.name: result_category
fields.code:
pick 'Two-point conversion made' when is_overtime_conversion and Scoring
      pick 'Two-point conversion failed' when is_overtime_conversion
      // ahead of both the defensive and the offensive touchdown: a kickoff
      // return is filed as the kicking team's own TD, and a punt return as
      // a plain defensive score
      pick 'Special teams touchdown' when is_special_teams_touchdown
      pick 'Defensive touchdown' when defensive_points_scored >= 6
      pick 'Safety' when defensive_points_scored = 2
      pick 'End of period' when DriveResult ? 'END OF HALF' | 'END OF GAME' | 'END OF 4TH QUARTER' | 'END OF HALF TD' | 'END OF GAME TD' | 'KICKOFF'
      pick 'Touchdown' when DriveResult = 'TD'
      pick 'Field goal' when DriveResult = 'FG'
      pick 'Punt' when DriveResult = 'PUNT'
      pick 'Missed field goal' when DriveResult = 'MISSED FG'
      pick 'Interception' when DriveResult = 'INT'
      pick 'Fumble' when DriveResult = 'FUMBLE'
      pick 'Turnover on downs' when DriveResult = 'DOWNS'
      pick 'Safety' when DriveResult = 'SF'
      else 'Uncategorized'

notes.text: #(index)

#(doc) How the drive ended, grouped into readable categories: Touchdown, Field goal, Punt, Missed field goal, Interception, Fumble, Turnover on downs, Safety, Defensive touchdown when the defense returned it for a score, End of period, Two-point conversion made and Two-point conversion failed for the alternating attempts from the third overtime on, and Uncategorized.

fields.name: result_abbreviation
fields.code:
pick '2PT' when result_category = 'Two-point conversion made'
      pick 'Miss' when result_category = 'Two-point conversion failed'
      pick 'ST TD' when result_category = 'Special teams touchdown'
      pick 'Def TD' when result_category = 'Defensive touchdown'
      // the clock running out on the game reads very differently from it
      // running out on the first half, so name them apart
      pick 'Game End' when result_category = 'End of period' and possessions.drives_left_in_game = 1
      pick 'Half' when result_category = 'End of period'
      pick 'TD' when result_category = 'Touchdown'
      pick 'FG' when result_category = 'Field goal'
      pick 'P' when result_category = 'Punt'
      pick 'FGA' when result_category = 'Missed field goal'
      pick 'Int' when result_category = 'Interception'
      pick 'Fum' when result_category = 'Fumble'
      pick 'Downs' when result_category = 'Turnover on downs'
      pick 'S' when result_category = 'Safety'
      else 'Other'

notes.text: #(doc) Short label for how the drive ended, for drive charts: TD, FG, P for punt, FGA for a missed field goal attempt, Int, Fum, Downs, S for safety, Def TD, Half when the first half ran out, Game End when the game ran out, 2PT for a converted overtime two-point attempt and Miss for one that failed, and Other.
#(doc) True when the offense scored a touchdown on this drive. False when the result string says TD but the points went to the defense.
#(doc) True when the drive ended in a made field goal by the offense. False for a kick that was blocked and returned.
#(doc) True when the drive ended in a punt.
#(doc) True when the offense turned the ball over by interception or fumble.
#(doc) True when the offense handed the ball over on downs.
#(doc) True when the drive ended in points for the offense, by touchdown or field goal.
#(doc) True when the drive gave up points to the defense, by return touchdown, blocked kick, or safety.

fields.name: is_kickoff_return_touchdown
fields.code:
DriveResult = 'TD' and Plays <= 1 and Yards >= 85 and Scoring
      and EndOffenseScore - StartOffenseScore = 0

notes.text:
#|(doc)
True when this row is really a kickoff return touchdown. The feed files one under the
KICKING team as a one-play "drive" covering nearly the whole field whose own score
never moves — Utah Tech at BYU in 2026 opens the second half with "Utah Tech, 1 play,
100 yards, TD", which was BYU running the kickoff back. Read as an ordinary touchdown
it credits the wrong team, in the wrong direction. The returning team is this row's
Defense.

fields.name: is_punt_return_touchdown
fields.code:
(DriveResult ? 'PUNT TD' | 'PUNT RETURN TD')
      or (DriveResult = 'PUNT' and defensive_points_scored >= 6)
      or (DriveResult = 'TD' and defensive_points_scored >= 6
          and Plays <= 4 and Yards < 15 and EndYardsToGoal = 100)

notes.text:
#|(doc)
True when the defending team ran a punt back for a touchdown, or blocked one and
returned it. Named outright by the feed on some rows (PUNT TD, PUNT RETURN TD); on the
rest it is a punt whose DEFENSE gained the points, or a short possession the feed calls
a TD that ends back on the offense's own goal line — the returner's end zone.

fields.name: is_blocked_kick_return_touchdown
fields.code:
DriveResult = 'MISSED FG TD'
      or ((DriveResult ? 'FG' | 'MISSED FG') and defensive_points_scored >= 6)

notes.text: #(doc) True when the defending team returned a blocked or missed field goal for a touchdown.
#(doc) True when the touchdown came on special teams — a kickoff return, a punt return, or a blocked kick — rather than from the offense or from a takeaway. The scoring team is this row's Defense.

fields.name: special_teams_score_type
fields.code:
pick 'Kickoff return' when is_kickoff_return_touchdown
      pick 'Punt return' when is_punt_return_touchdown
      pick 'Blocked kick return' when is_blocked_kick_return_touchdown
      else null

notes.text: #(doc) How a special-teams touchdown was scored: Kickoff return, Punt return, or Blocked kick return. Empty on every other drive.
#(doc) True when the drive ran three plays or fewer and ended in a punt, the classic three-and-out.
#(doc) True when the drive simply ran out of clock at the end of a half, a quarter, or the game.
#(doc) True when the drive gained 40 yards or more.

#|(doc)
True when the drive was a quality possession in the Eckel-rate sense: it scored a
touchdown, or it reached the opponent's 35 having gained at least ten yards. Eckel rate
proper counts a first down inside the opponent's 40, which needs play-by-play; ending
at the 35 or closer after a ten-yard gain is the drive-level stand-in.

fields.name: drive_points
fields.code:
pick EndOffenseScore - StartOffenseScore
        when EndOffenseScore - StartOffenseScore >= 0 and EndOffenseScore - StartOffenseScore <= 8
      pick 7 when DriveResult = 'TD'
      pick 3 when DriveResult = 'FG'
      else 0

notes.text:
#|(doc)
Points the offense scored on this drive, taken from the score before and after so that
extra points and two-point conversions are counted. On the 0.8% of drives where the
feed's score columns skip an intervening score and produce a value no single possession
can produce (outside 0 to 8), it falls back to the drive's result: 7 for a touchdown,
3 for a made field goal, 0 otherwise. Without that repair those 325 rows contribute 6%
of the season's points and inflate every scoring rate.

fields.name: is_named_defensive_score
fields.code:
DriveResult ? 'INT TD' | 'FUMBLE RETURN TD' | 'FUMBLE TD' | 'PUNT TD' | 'PUNT RETURN TD'
        | 'MISSED FG TD' | 'DOWNS TD' | 'END OF HALF TD' | 'END OF GAME TD' | 'SF'

notes.text: #(doc) True when the feed's own result string already says the defense scored, for example INT TD, PUNT RETURN TD, or SF.

fields.name: scoreboard_agrees_with_next_drive
fields.code:
possessions.next_offense is null
      or (possessions.next_offense != Offense
          and EndOffenseScore = possessions.next_start_defense_score
          and EndDefenseScore = possessions.next_start_offense_score)
      or (possessions.next_offense = Offense
          and EndOffenseScore = possessions.next_start_offense_score
          and EndDefenseScore = possessions.next_start_defense_score)

notes.text:
#|(doc)
True when this drive's closing scoreboard matches the next drive's opening one, with the
two teams' columns swapped if possession changed hands. Roughly 7% of consecutive drives
disagree, which is the feed's score columns lagging a possession — so this is what
separates a real defensive score from a column that simply jumped.

fields.name: defensive_points_scored
fields.code:
pick EndDefenseScore - StartDefenseScore
        when ((EndDefenseScore - StartDefenseScore >= 6 and EndDefenseScore - StartDefenseScore <= 8)
              or EndDefenseScore - StartDefenseScore = 2)
         and (is_named_defensive_score or scoreboard_agrees_with_next_drive)
      pick 2 when DriveResult = 'SF'
      pick 7 when is_named_defensive_score
      else 0

notes.text:
#|(doc)
Points the defense scored on this possession, from return touchdowns, blocked kicks
returned, and safeties. Read from the scoreboard rather than the result string, which
says how a possession ended and not who scored.

Two guardrails, both earned the hard way. A defense cannot score 3, so only a move of
6 to 8 counts as a return touchdown and only 2 as a safety. And a scoreboard move the
feed does not corroborate is not believed: of the 231 drives where the defensive column
jumps by a touchdown without the result string saying so, only 122 line up with the next
drive's opening score — the rest are the columns lagging, and counting them would invent
about a hundred defensive touchdowns.
#(doc) Kept as an alias of the points the defense scored on this possession.

fields.name: defensive_score_type
fields.code:
pick null when defensive_points_scored = 0
      pick 'Safety' when defensive_points_scored = 2
      pick 'Punt return or block' when DriveResult ? 'PUNT' | 'PUNT TD' | 'PUNT RETURN TD'
      pick 'Interception return' when DriveResult ? 'INT' | 'INT TD'
      pick 'Fumble return' when DriveResult ? 'FUMBLE' | 'FUMBLE TD' | 'FUMBLE RETURN TD'
      pick 'Blocked kick return' when DriveResult ? 'FG' | 'MISSED FG' | 'MISSED FG TD'
      else 'Return touchdown'

notes.text:
#|(doc)
Distance to the end zone where the OFFENSE's possession actually ended: its starting
distance less the net yards it gained, clamped into the field of play.

Not the feed's EndYardsToGoal, which on a kick or a return is where the BALL came to
rest afterwards. A punt is the clearest case: Arizona's 3-play, minus-14-yard
possession at BYU in 2026 starts on its own 25 and the feed ends it on BYU's 11, 64
yards downfield — the punt. Drawn from the feed the drive reads as a 64-yard march
instead of a three-and-out that lost ground. About a fifth of punts differ this way,
by a punt's distance (34 to 46 yards), and interceptions differ by their return.

Field stripe a return touchdown started from, in absolute field coordinates.

On a KICKOFF return the feed gives the return's length in Yards (100 for BYU's

fields.name: losing_team_possessions_left
fields.code:
pick possessions.offense_possessions_left when margin_at_drive_start < 0
      pick possessions.drives_left_in_game - possessions.offense_possessions_left when margin_at_drive_start > 0
      else null

notes.text: #(doc) Number of possessions the trailing team has left to erase the deficit. Empty when the game is tied.
#(doc) True when this is the last possession of the game.
#(doc) True when this is the last possession of the first half.
#(doc) True when this is the last possession of regulation, the end of the second half.

fields.name: clock_ran_out
fields.code:
not is_turnover
      and not is_turnover_on_downs
      and not is_field_goal_attempt
      and EndOffenseScore = StartOffenseScore
      and EndDefenseScore = StartDefenseScore

notes.text: #(doc) True when the possession simply ran out of clock: no turnover, no points for either team, and no field goal attempt.

fields.name: is_garbage_end_of_half
fields.code:
Plays <= 2 and clock_ran_out
      and (ends_first_half or (ends_regulation and margin_at_drive_start = 0))

notes.text: #(doc) Garbage rule one: a possession of two plays or fewer that runs out the clock to end the first half, or to end regulation with the score tied, without a turnover, a score, or a field goal attempt.

fields.name: is_garbage_out_of_reach
fields.code:
StartPeriod >= 3
      and margin_at_drive_start != 0
      and 8 * losing_team_possessions_left + 1 < deficit_at_drive_start

notes.text: #(doc) Garbage rule two: a second-half possession where the game is already out of reach, because eight points times the trailing team's remaining possessions, plus one, is still less than the deficit.

fields.name: is_garbage_trailing_kneel
fields.code: Plays <= 2 and ends_game and clock_ran_out and margin_at_drive_start < -8

notes.text: #(doc) Garbage rule three: a possession of two plays or fewer by a team trailing by more than eight that runs out the clock to end the game.

fields.name: is_garbage_victory_formation
fields.code:
ends_game and clock_ran_out
      and margin_at_drive_start > 0 and margin_at_drive_start <= 8

notes.text: #(doc) Garbage rule four: the victory formation. A possession by the team ahead by eight points or fewer that runs out the clock to end the game.

fields.name: is_garbage_possession
fields.code:
(is_garbage_end_of_half
        or is_garbage_out_of_reach
        or is_garbage_trailing_kneel
        or is_garbage_victory_formation) ?? false

notes.text:
#|(doc)
True when the possession is garbage time — neither team is still playing to win it.
Covers all four of BCFtoys' rules: a kneel-down to end the first half or a tied
regulation, a second-half possession with the game already out of reach, a kneel-down
by a team trailing by more than eight, and the winning team's victory formation.
About 16% of the season's drives, and half of all fourth-quarter possessions.

fields.name: garbage_reason
fields.code:
pick 'End of half kneel-down' when is_garbage_end_of_half
      pick 'Victory formation' when is_garbage_victory_formation

fields.name: is_overtime_conversion
fields.code: StartPeriod >= 5 and DriveResult = 'Uncategorized' and Plays <= 1 and Yards = 0

notes.text:
#|(doc)
True when this possession is an overtime two-point conversion attempt rather than a
drive. From the third overtime on, the rules stop giving each team a possession from
the opponent's 25 and give it a single snap from the 3 instead, alternating until one
team converts and the other does not.

The feed has no name for these. It files all nine of them under the literal result
string "Uncategorized", every one a single play that gains nothing — and that pair of
facts, inside overtime, identifies them exactly. Period alone will not do it: the
feed skips a period in Missouri-Auburn and labels an ordinary 7-play touchdown drive
as the seventh period.

#(doc) True when an overtime two-point conversion attempt was good. Read from the feed's Scoring flag, which tracks these correctly — it reproduces the 53-51 finish of the nine-period South Dakota game exactly.

fields.name: result_category
fields.code:
pick 'Two-point conversion made' when is_overtime_conversion and Scoring
      pick 'Two-point conversion failed' when is_overtime_conversion
      // ahead of both the defensive and the offensive touchdown: a kickoff
      // return is filed as the kicking team's own TD, and a punt return as
      // a plain defensive score
      pick 'Special teams touchdown' when is_special_teams_touchdown
      pick 'Defensive touchdown' when defensive_points_scored >= 6
      pick 'Safety' when defensive_points_scored = 2
      pick 'End of period' when DriveResult ? 'END OF HALF' | 'END OF GAME' | 'END OF 4TH QUARTER' | 'END OF HALF TD' | 'END OF GAME TD' | 'KICKOFF'
      pick 'Touchdown' when DriveResult = 'TD'
      pick 'Field goal' when DriveResult = 'FG'
      pick 'Punt' when DriveResult = 'PUNT'
      pick 'Missed field goal' when DriveResult = 'MISSED FG'
      pick 'Interception' when DriveResult = 'INT'
      pick 'Fumble' when DriveResult = 'FUMBLE'
      pick 'Turnover on downs' when DriveResult = 'DOWNS'
      pick 'Safety' when DriveResult = 'SF'
      else 'Uncategorized'

notes.text: #(index)

#(doc) How the drive ended, grouped into readable categories: Touchdown, Field goal, Punt, Missed field goal, Interception, Fumble, Turnover on downs, Safety, Defensive touchdown when the defense returned it for a score, End of period, Two-point conversion made and Two-point conversion failed for the alternating attempts from the third overtime on, and Uncategorized.

fields.name: result_abbreviation
fields.code:
pick '2PT' when result_category = 'Two-point conversion made'
      pick 'Miss' when result_category = 'Two-point conversion failed'
      pick 'ST TD' when result_category = 'Special teams touchdown'
      pick 'Def TD' when result_category = 'Defensive touchdown'
      // the clock running out on the game reads very differently from it
      // running out on the first half, so name them apart
      pick 'Game End' when result_category = 'End of period' and possessions.drives_left_in_game = 1
      pick 'Half' when result_category = 'End of period'
      pick 'TD' when result_category = 'Touchdown'
      pick 'FG' when result_category = 'Field goal'
      pick 'P' when result_category = 'Punt'
      pick 'FGA' when result_category = 'Missed field goal'
      pick 'Int' when result_category = 'Interception'
      pick 'Fum' when result_category = 'Fumble'
      pick 'Downs' when result_category = 'Turnover on downs'
      pick 'S' when result_category = 'Safety'
      else 'Other'

notes.text: #(doc) Short label for how the drive ended, for drive charts: TD, FG, P for punt, FGA for a missed field goal attempt, Int, Fum, Downs, S for safety, Def TD, Half when the first half ran out, Game End when the game ran out, 2PT for a converted overtime two-point attempt and Miss for one that failed, and Other.
#(doc) True when the offense scored a touchdown on this drive. False when the result string says TD but the points went to the defense.
#(doc) True when the drive ended in a made field goal by the offense. False for a kick that was blocked and returned.
#(doc) True when the drive ended in a punt.
#(doc) True when the offense turned the ball over by interception or fumble.
#(doc) True when the offense handed the ball over on downs.
#(doc) True when the drive ended in points for the offense, by touchdown or field goal.
#(doc) True when the drive gave up points to the defense, by return touchdown, blocked kick, or safety.

fields.name: is_kickoff_return_touchdown
fields.code:
DriveResult = 'TD' and Plays <= 1 and Yards >= 85 and Scoring
      and EndOffenseScore - StartOffenseScore = 0

notes.text:
#|(doc)
True when this row is really a kickoff return touchdown. The feed files one under the
KICKING team as a one-play "drive" covering nearly the whole field whose own score
never moves — Utah Tech at BYU in 2026 opens the second half with "Utah Tech, 1 play,
100 yards, TD", which was BYU running the kickoff back. Read as an ordinary touchdown
it credits the wrong team, in the wrong direction. The returning team is this row's
Defense.

fields.name: is_punt_return_touchdown
fields.code:
(DriveResult ? 'PUNT TD' | 'PUNT RETURN TD')
      or (DriveResult = 'PUNT' and defensive_points_scored >= 6)
      or (DriveResult = 'TD' and defensive_points_scored >= 6
          and Plays <= 4 and Yards < 15 and EndYardsToGoal = 100)

notes.text:
#|(doc)
True when the defending team ran a punt back for a touchdown, or blocked one and
returned it. Named outright by the feed on some rows (PUNT TD, PUNT RETURN TD); on the
rest it is a punt whose DEFENSE gained the points, or a short possession the feed calls
a TD that ends back on the offense's own goal line — the returner's end zone.

fields.name: is_blocked_kick_return_touchdown
fields.code:
DriveResult = 'MISSED FG TD'
      or ((DriveResult ? 'FG' | 'MISSED FG') and defensive_points_scored >= 6)

notes.text: #(doc) True when the defending team returned a blocked or missed field goal for a touchdown.
#(doc) True when the touchdown came on special teams — a kickoff return, a punt return, or a blocked kick — rather than from the offense or from a takeaway. The scoring team is this row's Defense.

fields.name: special_teams_score_type
fields.code:
pick 'Kickoff return' when is_kickoff_return_touchdown
      pick 'Punt return' when is_punt_return_touchdown
      pick 'Blocked kick return' when is_blocked_kick_return_touchdown
      else null

notes.text: #(doc) How a special-teams touchdown was scored: Kickoff return, Punt return, or Blocked kick return. Empty on every other drive.
#(doc) True when the drive ran three plays or fewer and ended in a punt, the classic three-and-out.
#(doc) True when the drive simply ran out of clock at the end of a half, a quarter, or the game.
#(doc) True when the drive gained 40 yards or more.

#|(doc)
True when the drive was a quality possession in the Eckel-rate sense: it scored a
touchdown, or it reached the opponent's 35 having gained at least ten yards. Eckel rate
proper counts a first down inside the opponent's 40, which needs play-by-play; ending
at the 35 or closer after a ten-yard gain is the drive-level stand-in.

fields.name: drive_points
fields.code:
pick EndOffenseScore - StartOffenseScore
        when EndOffenseScore - StartOffenseScore >= 0 and EndOffenseScore - StartOffenseScore <= 8
      pick 7 when DriveResult = 'TD'
      pick 3 when DriveResult = 'FG'
      else 0

notes.text:
#|(doc)
Points the offense scored on this drive, taken from the score before and after so that
extra points and two-point conversions are counted. On the 0.8% of drives where the
feed's score columns skip an intervening score and produce a value no single possession
can produce (outside 0 to 8), it falls back to the drive's result: 7 for a touchdown,
3 for a made field goal, 0 otherwise. Without that repair those 325 rows contribute 6%
of the season's points and inflate every scoring rate.

fields.name: is_named_defensive_score
fields.code:
DriveResult ? 'INT TD' | 'FUMBLE RETURN TD' | 'FUMBLE TD' | 'PUNT TD' | 'PUNT RETURN TD'
        | 'MISSED FG TD' | 'DOWNS TD' | 'END OF HALF TD' | 'END OF GAME TD' | 'SF'

notes.text: #(doc) True when the feed's own result string already says the defense scored, for example INT TD, PUNT RETURN TD, or SF.

fields.name: scoreboard_agrees_with_next_drive
fields.code:
possessions.next_offense is null
      or (possessions.next_offense != Offense
          and EndOffenseScore = possessions.next_start_defense_score
          and EndDefenseScore = possessions.next_start_offense_score)
      or (possessions.next_offense = Offense
          and EndOffenseScore = possessions.next_start_offense_score
          and EndDefenseScore = possessions.next_start_defense_score)

notes.text:
#|(doc)
True when this drive's closing scoreboard matches the next drive's opening one, with the
two teams' columns swapped if possession changed hands. Roughly 7% of consecutive drives
disagree, which is the feed's score columns lagging a possession — so this is what
separates a real defensive score from a column that simply jumped.

fields.name: defensive_points_scored
fields.code:
pick EndDefenseScore - StartDefenseScore
        when ((EndDefenseScore - StartDefenseScore >= 6 and EndDefenseScore - StartDefenseScore <= 8)
              or EndDefenseScore - StartDefenseScore = 2)
         and (is_named_defensive_score or scoreboard_agrees_with_next_drive)
      pick 2 when DriveResult = 'SF'
      pick 7 when is_named_defensive_score
      else 0

notes.text:
#|(doc)
Points the defense scored on this possession, from return touchdowns, blocked kicks
returned, and safeties. Read from the scoreboard rather than the result string, which
says how a possession ended and not who scored.

Two guardrails, both earned the hard way. A defense cannot score 3, so only a move of
6 to 8 counts as a return touchdown and only 2 as a safety. And a scoreboard move the
feed does not corroborate is not believed: of the 231 drives where the defensive column
jumps by a touchdown without the result string saying so, only 122 line up with the next
drive's opening score — the rest are the columns lagging, and counting them would invent
about a hundred defensive touchdowns.
#(doc) Kept as an alias of the points the defense scored on this possession.

fields.name: defensive_score_type
fields.code:
pick null when defensive_points_scored = 0
      pick 'Safety' when defensive_points_scored = 2
      pick 'Punt return or block' when DriveResult ? 'PUNT' | 'PUNT TD' | 'PUNT RETURN TD'
      pick 'Interception return' when DriveResult ? 'INT' | 'INT TD'
      pick 'Fumble return' when DriveResult ? 'FUMBLE' | 'FUMBLE TD' | 'FUMBLE RETURN TD'
      pick 'Blocked kick return' when DriveResult ? 'FG' | 'MISSED FG' | 'MISSED FG TD'
      else 'Return touchdown'

fields.code:
pick '1st' when StartPeriod = 1
      pick '2nd' when StartPeriod = 2
      pick '3rd' when StartPeriod = 3
      pick '4th' when StartPeriod = 4
      pick 'OT' when StartPeriod >= 5
      else 'Unknown'

fields.code:
pick '1st half' when StartPeriod <= 2
      pick '2nd half' when StartPeriod = 3 or StartPeriod = 4
      pick 'Overtime' when StartPeriod >= 5
      else 'Unknown'

fields.name: field_goal_distance
fields.code:
pick EndYardsToGoal + 17 when is_field_goal_attempt
      else null

notes.text: #(doc) Length of the field goal attempt in yards, counted from the holder's spot through the back of the end zone: the ball's distance to the goal line plus 17. Empty on drives that did not end in a kick.

fields.name: field_goal_distance_band
fields.code:
pick floor((EndYardsToGoal + 17) / 5) * 5 + 2.5 when is_field_goal_attempt
      else null

notes.text: #(doc) Field goal distance rounded into five-yard bands and labelled with the middle of the band, so 42.5 covers attempts from 40 to 44 yards. Use it when comparing kicking curves for groups smaller than the whole league, where single-yard buckets are too thin.

fields.name: field_goal_range
fields.code:
pick null when not is_field_goal_attempt
      pick 'Chip shot' when EndYardsToGoal + 17 < 30
      pick 'Short' when EndYardsToGoal + 17 < 40
      pick 'Medium' when EndYardsToGoal + 17 < 50
      pick 'Long' when EndYardsToGoal + 17 < 60
      else 'Very long'

notes.text:
#|(doc)
Distance to the end zone where the OFFENSE's possession actually ended: its starting
distance less the net yards it gained, clamped into the field of play.

Not the feed's EndYardsToGoal, which on a kick or a return is where the BALL came to
rest afterwards. A punt is the clearest case: Arizona's 3-play, minus-14-yard
possession at BYU in 2026 starts on its own 25 and the feed ends it on BYU's 11, 64
yards downfield — the punt. Drawn from the feed the drive reads as a 64-yard march
instead of a three-and-out that lost ground. About a fifth of punts differ this way,
by a punt's distance (34 to 46 yards), and interceptions differ by their return.

fields.name: chart_end_yardline
fields.code:
pick 100 when is_touchdown and IsHomeOffense
      pick 0 when is_touchdown and not IsHomeOffense
      pick 100 - chart_end_yards_to_goal when IsHomeOffense
      else chart_end_yards_to_goal

notes.text:
#|(doc)
Field stripe a return touchdown started from, in absolute field coordinates.

On a KICKOFF return the feed gives the return's length in Yards (100 for BYU's
second-half return against Utah Tech in 2026), and the returning team is this row's
Defense, so the return is drawn its true length back from the goal line it reached.
A punt or blocked-kick return has no return yardage anywhere in the feed — only the
possession that preceded it — so it starts where that possession ended, which is a
floor on the return, not its real length.
#(doc) Direction the offense was moving on the field chart: up toward 100 for the home team, down toward 0 for the away team.
#(doc) Score margin from the point of view of the team with the ball, as it stood when the drive began. Positive means the offense was ahead.
#(doc) Points the trailing team was behind by when the drive began. Zero when the game was tied.
#(doc) Number of possessions the team with the ball has left in the game, counting this one.
#(doc) Number of possessions the defending team has left in the game after this one.

fields.name: losing_team_possessions_left
fields.code:
pick possessions.offense_possessions_left when margin_at_drive_start < 0
      pick possessions.drives_left_in_game - possessions.offense_possessions_left when margin_at_drive_start > 0
      else null

notes.text: #(doc) Number of possessions the trailing team has left to erase the deficit. Empty when the game is tied.
#(doc) True when this is the last possession of the game.
#(doc) True when this is the last possession of the first half.
#(doc) True when this is the last possession of regulation, the end of the second half.

fields.name: clock_ran_out
fields.code:
not is_turnover
      and not is_turnover_on_downs
      and not is_field_goal_attempt
      and EndOffenseScore = StartOffenseScore
      and EndDefenseScore = StartDefenseScore

notes.text: #(doc) True when the possession simply ran out of clock: no turnover, no points for either team, and no field goal attempt.

fields.name: is_garbage_end_of_half
fields.code:
Plays <= 2 and clock_ran_out
      and (ends_first_half or (ends_regulation and margin_at_drive_start = 0))

notes.text: #(doc) Garbage rule one: a possession of two plays or fewer that runs out the clock to end the first half, or to end regulation with the score tied, without a turnover, a score, or a field goal attempt.

fields.name: is_garbage_out_of_reach
fields.code:
StartPeriod >= 3
      and margin_at_drive_start != 0
      and 8 * losing_team_possessions_left + 1 < deficit_at_drive_start

notes.text: #(doc) Garbage rule two: a second-half possession where the game is already out of reach, because eight points times the trailing team's remaining possessions, plus one, is still less than the deficit.

fields.name: is_garbage_trailing_kneel
fields.code: Plays <= 2 and ends_game and clock_ran_out and margin_at_drive_start < -8

notes.text: #(doc) Garbage rule three: a possession of two plays or fewer by a team trailing by more than eight that runs out the clock to end the game.

fields.name: is_garbage_victory_formation
fields.code:
ends_game and clock_ran_out
      and margin_at_drive_start > 0 and margin_at_drive_start <= 8

notes.text: #(doc) Garbage rule four: the victory formation. A possession by the team ahead by eight points or fewer that runs out the clock to end the game.

fields.name: is_garbage_possession
fields.code:
(is_garbage_end_of_half
        or is_garbage_out_of_reach
        or is_garbage_trailing_kneel
        or is_garbage_victory_formation) ?? false

notes.text:
#|(doc)
True when the possession is garbage time — neither team is still playing to win it.
Covers all four of BCFtoys' rules: a kneel-down to end the first half or a tied
regulation, a second-half possession with the game already out of reach, a kneel-down
by a team trailing by more than eight, and the winning team's victory formation.
About 16% of the season's drives, and half of all fourth-quarter possessions.

fields.name: garbage_reason
fields.code:
pick 'End of half kneel-down' when is_garbage_end_of_half
      pick 'Victory formation' when is_garbage_victory_formation
      pick 'Trailing kneel-down' when is_garbage_trailing_kneel
      pick 'Out of reach' when is_garbage_out_of_reach
      else 'Competitive'

fields.code:

      / nullif(count() { where: not is_garbage_possession }, 0)

blockNotes.text:
#|(doc)
One row per college football game in the 2025 and 2026 seasons, with every drive of that
game joined in. Carries the final score, line score, venue, conferences, Elo, CFBD's
excitement rating and a box-score thrill index, plus drive-level totals. Use it for
schedules, results, the most exciting games, and game summaries.

#|(doc)
One row per college football game in the 2025 and 2026 seasons, across every division: FBS, FCS, Division II
and Division III. Each game carries the final score, venue and announced attendance,
the conference and division of both teams, pregame and postgame Elo ratings, postgame
win probability, an excitement rating, and College Football Playoff bracket details
for playoff games. Use it for schedules, results, margins, attendance, rankings-style
Elo movement, and as the game-level context for drive-by-drive data, which joins on
game id.
#(doc) Games with the thrill index itself as a column.

notes.text: #(doc) Announced attendance for the game, in people. Missing for many games, especially at the Division II and Division III level.
#(index)
#(doc) Division the away team competes in: fbs, fcs, ii for Division II, or iii for Division III.
#(index)
#(doc) Conference the away team belongs to, for example SEC, Big Ten, ACC or Big 12. Missing for independents and some non-Division-I programs.
#(doc) Unique identifier of the away team.
#(doc) Points the away team scored in each period, as a comma-separated list in order, for example 3,7,7,0 for the four quarters.
#(doc) Final points scored by the away team. Missing until the game has been played.
#(doc) Away team's Elo power rating after the game, reflecting the result. Higher is stronger.
#(doc) Postgame win expectancy for the away team: how likely it was to win given how the game was played, from 0 to 1. It pairs with the home value to sum to 1 and is not the result itself.
#(doc) Away team's Elo power rating going into the game. Higher is stronger; roughly 1500 is average.
#(index)
#(doc) Name of the away team, for example Michigan or Texas.
#(doc) True when the game has been played and the final score is official.
#(doc) True when both teams belong to the same conference, so the result counts in the conference standings.
#(doc) Excitement rating for the game, built from how much and how often the win probability swung. Typical games rate near 4; the wildest finishes rate above 8.
#(doc) Link to the game's video highlights, when one is published.
#(index)
#(doc) Division the home team competes in: fbs, fcs, ii for Division II, or iii for Division III.
#(index)
#(doc) Conference the home team belongs to, for example SEC, Big Ten, ACC or Big 12. Missing for independents and some non-Division-I programs.
#(doc) Unique identifier of the home team.
#(doc) Points the home team scored in each period, as a comma-separated list in order, for example 7,10,0,14 for the four quarters.
#(doc) Final points scored by the home team. Missing until the game has been played.
#(doc) Home team's Elo power rating after the game, reflecting the result. Higher is stronger.

#(doc) Postgame win expectancy for the home team: how likely it was to win given how the game was played, from 0 to 1. It pairs with the away value to sum to 1 and is not the result itself — a team can lose a game it was 90% likely to win. Matches the actual winner in about 90% of games.
#(doc) Home team's Elo power rating going into the game. Higher is stronger; roughly 1500 is average.
#(index)
#(doc) Name of the home team, for example Alabama or Ohio State.
#(doc) Unique identifier for the game. Join key to the drives data, whose GameId column holds the same value.
#(doc) True when the game was played at a neutral venue rather than either team's own stadium. Bowl games, playoff games and kickoff classics are typically neutral site.
#(doc) Free-text note about the game, usually the name of a kickoff event or a special circumstance, for example Aer Lingus College Football Classic.
#(doc) Playoff seed of the away team, 1 through 12. Missing outside the playoff.
#(index)
#(doc) Bowl the playoff game was hosted by, for example Rose Bowl, Sugar Bowl or College Football Playoff National Championship.
#(doc) Slot the game occupies in the playoff bracket, for example QF1 for the first quarterfinal or CH for the championship.
#(index)
#(doc) Postseason competition the game belongs to. cfp for the College Football Playoff; missing for regular-season and ordinary bowl games.
#(doc) Playoff bracket format in force for the season, for example twelve_team_2025.
#(doc) Playoff seed of the home team, 1 through 12. Missing outside the playoff.
#(index)
#(doc) Playoff round in machine form: first_round, quarterfinal, semifinal or championship.
#(index)
#(doc) Playoff round in readable form: First Round, Quarterfinal, Semifinal or National Championship.
#(doc) Season year the game belongs to: 2025 or 2026. A season's bowls and playoff games played in January still belong to the season that started in August.
#(index)
#(doc) Portion of the season: regular for the regular season, postseason for bowls and College Football Playoff games.
#(doc) Scheduled kickoff date and time, expressed in US Pacific local time.
#(doc) True when the kickoff time had not been announced yet, so only the date is meaningful.
#(index)
#(doc) Name of the stadium the game was played in, for example Bryant-Denny Stadium.
#(doc) Unique identifier of the stadium the game was played in.
#(doc) Week of the season the game was played in, numbered within the season type. Regular-season weeks run 1 to 16; postseason bowl and playoff games carry their own week numbers.
#(doc) Calendar date the game kicked off, in US Pacific local time.
#(doc) Matchup in away-at-home form, for example Michigan at Ohio State.

fields.name: final_score
fields.code:
pick concat(HomeTeam, ' ', HomePoints::string, ', ', AwayTeam, ' ', AwayPoints::string) when HomePoints >= AwayPoints
      else concat(AwayTeam, ' ', AwayPoints::string, ', ', HomeTeam, ' ', HomePoints::string)

notes.text: #(doc) Final score written out, for example Ohio State 30, Michigan 24, with the winner first. Empty until the game is played.

fields.name: winner
fields.code:
pick HomeTeam when HomePoints > AwayPoints
      pick AwayTeam when AwayPoints > HomePoints
      else null

notes.text: #(doc) Team that won the game. Empty for ties and for games that have not been played.

fields.name: loser
fields.code:
pick AwayTeam when HomePoints > AwayPoints
      pick HomeTeam when AwayPoints > HomePoints
      else null

notes.text: #(doc) Team that lost the game. Empty for ties and for games that have not been played.
#(doc) True when the home team won.
#(doc) Combined points scored by both teams.
#(doc) Home points minus away points. Positive when the home team won, negative when the away team won.
#(doc) Winning margin in points, regardless of which team won.

fields.name: margin_bucket
fields.code:
pick 'One-score game' when abs(HomePoints - AwayPoints) <= 8
      pick 'Two-score game' when abs(HomePoints - AwayPoints) <= 16
      pick 'Comfortable' when abs(HomePoints - AwayPoints) <= 27
      else 'Blowout'

notes.text: #(doc) How close the game was: One-score game for a margin of 8 or less, Two-score game for 9 to 16, Comfortable for 17 to 27, and Blowout for 28 or more.
#(doc) Division matchup, for example fbs vs fbs or fbs vs fcs, using the two teams' divisions.
#(doc) True when both teams are FBS programs, the top division of college football.
#(doc) True when the game is part of the College Football Playoff bracket.
#(doc) Home team's Elo rating minus the away team's Elo rating before kickoff. Positive means the home team was the stronger team on paper.

fields.name: elo_favorite
fields.code:
pick HomeTeam when HomePregameElo > AwayPregameElo
      pick AwayTeam when AwayPregameElo > HomePregameElo
      else null

notes.text: #(doc) Team the pregame Elo ratings favored, before any home-field adjustment.

fields.name: is_elo_upset
fields.code:
(HomePoints > AwayPoints and HomePregameElo < AwayPregameElo)
      or (AwayPoints > HomePoints and AwayPregameElo < HomePregameElo)

notes.text: #(doc) True when the team with the lower pregame Elo rating won the game.
#(doc) Points of Elo rating the home team gained from the game. Negative when the home team lost ground.
#(doc) Points of Elo rating the away team gained from the game. Negative when the away team lost ground.

fields.name: excitement_tier
fields.code:
pick 'Instant classic' when ExcitementIndex > 8
      pick 'Thriller' when ExcitementIndex > 6
      pick 'Competitive' when ExcitementIndex > 4
      else 'Routine'

notes.text: #(doc) How dramatic the game was, from its excitement rating: Instant classic above 8, Thriller above 6, Competitive above 4, and Routine at 4 or below.
#(doc) Season year as text, for example 2026. What the season picker filters on.
#(doc) The week as a reader names it: Week 1 through Week 16 in the regular season, and Postseason for every bowl and College Football Playoff game.
#(doc) Sort key for week_label, so Week 10 follows Week 9 and the postseason comes last.
#(doc) Number of periods the game went, from the line score: 4 for regulation, 5 or more when it went to overtime.
#(doc) True when the game went to overtime.
#(doc) Home team's points through three quarters, from the line score.
#(doc) Away team's points through three quarters, from the line score.
#(doc) Home points minus away points going into the fourth quarter. Positive when the home team led.
#(doc) True when the eventual winner was behind going into the fourth quarter.
#(doc) Thrill index points for how close the final score was: 35 for a one-possession finish at a margin of zero, falling to 0 at a 28-point margin.
#(doc) Thrill index points for how close the game was going into the fourth quarter: 20 when tied, falling to 0 at a 17-point margin. Zero when the line score is missing.
#(doc) Thrill index points for a comeback: 10 when the winner trailed after three quarters.
#(doc) Thrill index points for overtime: 15 when the game went past regulation.
#(doc) Thrill index points for scoring: up to 12, reached at 80 combined points.
#(doc) Thrill index points for an upset: up to 10 when the team with the lower pregame Elo won, full marks at a 250-point rating gap.
#(doc) Thrill index points for stakes: 8 for a College Football Playoff game.

#|(doc)
How exciting the game was, from 0 to 100, built from the box score so every completed
game has one: how close the final was, how close it was entering the fourth quarter,
whether the winner came from behind, overtime, combined scoring, an Elo upset, and
playoff stakes. Around 25 is a routine game; above 75 is an instant classic. Empty
until the game is played.

fields.name: thrill_tier
fields.code:
pick null when calc_thrill_index is null
      pick 'Instant classic' when calc_thrill_index >= 75
      pick 'Thriller' when calc_thrill_index >= 55
      pick 'Good game' when calc_thrill_index >= 35
      else 'Routine'

fields.name: is_overtime_conversion
fields.code: StartPeriod >= 5 and DriveResult = 'Uncategorized' and Plays <= 1 and Yards = 0

notes.text:
#|(doc)
True when this possession is an overtime two-point conversion attempt rather than a
drive. From the third overtime on, the rules stop giving each team a possession from
the opponent's 25 and give it a single snap from the 3 instead, alternating until one
team converts and the other does not.

The feed has no name for these. It files all nine of them under the literal result
string "Uncategorized", every one a single play that gains nothing — and that pair of
facts, inside overtime, identifies them exactly. Period alone will not do it: the
feed skips a period in Missouri-Auburn and labels an ordinary 7-play touchdown drive
as the seventh period.

#(doc) True when an overtime two-point conversion attempt was good. Read from the feed's Scoring flag, which tracks these correctly — it reproduces the 53-51 finish of the nine-period South Dakota game exactly.

fields.name: result_category
fields.code:
pick 'Two-point conversion made' when is_overtime_conversion and Scoring
      pick 'Two-point conversion failed' when is_overtime_conversion
      // ahead of both the defensive and the offensive touchdown: a kickoff
      // return is filed as the kicking team's own TD, and a punt return as
      // a plain defensive score
      pick 'Special teams touchdown' when is_special_teams_touchdown
      pick 'Defensive touchdown' when defensive_points_scored >= 6
      pick 'Safety' when defensive_points_scored = 2
      pick 'End of period' when DriveResult ? 'END OF HALF' | 'END OF GAME' | 'END OF 4TH QUARTER' | 'END OF HALF TD' | 'END OF GAME TD' | 'KICKOFF'
      pick 'Touchdown' when DriveResult = 'TD'
      pick 'Field goal' when DriveResult = 'FG'
      pick 'Punt' when DriveResult = 'PUNT'
      pick 'Missed field goal' when DriveResult = 'MISSED FG'
      pick 'Interception' when DriveResult = 'INT'
      pick 'Fumble' when DriveResult = 'FUMBLE'
      pick 'Turnover on downs' when DriveResult = 'DOWNS'
      pick 'Safety' when DriveResult = 'SF'
      else 'Uncategorized'

notes.text: #(index)

#(doc) How the drive ended, grouped into readable categories: Touchdown, Field goal, Punt, Missed field goal, Interception, Fumble, Turnover on downs, Safety, Defensive touchdown when the defense returned it for a score, End of period, Two-point conversion made and Two-point conversion failed for the alternating attempts from the third overtime on, and Uncategorized.

fields.name: result_abbreviation
fields.code:
pick '2PT' when result_category = 'Two-point conversion made'
      pick 'Miss' when result_category = 'Two-point conversion failed'
      pick 'ST TD' when result_category = 'Special teams touchdown'
      pick 'Def TD' when result_category = 'Defensive touchdown'
      // the clock running out on the game reads very differently from it
      // running out on the first half, so name them apart
      pick 'Game End' when result_category = 'End of period' and possessions.drives_left_in_game = 1
      pick 'Half' when result_category = 'End of period'
      pick 'TD' when result_category = 'Touchdown'
      pick 'FG' when result_category = 'Field goal'
      pick 'P' when result_category = 'Punt'
      pick 'FGA' when result_category = 'Missed field goal'
      pick 'Int' when result_category = 'Interception'
      pick 'Fum' when result_category = 'Fumble'
      pick 'Downs' when result_category = 'Turnover on downs'
      pick 'S' when result_category = 'Safety'
      else 'Other'

notes.text: #(doc) Short label for how the drive ended, for drive charts: TD, FG, P for punt, FGA for a missed field goal attempt, Int, Fum, Downs, S for safety, Def TD, Half when the first half ran out, Game End when the game ran out, 2PT for a converted overtime two-point attempt and Miss for one that failed, and Other.
#(doc) True when the offense scored a touchdown on this drive. False when the result string says TD but the points went to the defense.
#(doc) True when the drive ended in a made field goal by the offense. False for a kick that was blocked and returned.
#(doc) True when the drive ended in a punt.
#(doc) True when the offense turned the ball over by interception or fumble.
#(doc) True when the offense handed the ball over on downs.
#(doc) True when the drive ended in points for the offense, by touchdown or field goal.
#(doc) True when the drive gave up points to the defense, by return touchdown, blocked kick, or safety.

fields.name: is_kickoff_return_touchdown
fields.code:
DriveResult = 'TD' and Plays <= 1 and Yards >= 85 and Scoring
      and EndOffenseScore - StartOffenseScore = 0

notes.text:
#|(doc)
True when this row is really a kickoff return touchdown. The feed files one under the
KICKING team as a one-play "drive" covering nearly the whole field whose own score
never moves — Utah Tech at BYU in 2026 opens the second half with "Utah Tech, 1 play,
100 yards, TD", which was BYU running the kickoff back. Read as an ordinary touchdown
it credits the wrong team, in the wrong direction. The returning team is this row's
Defense.

fields.name: is_punt_return_touchdown
fields.code:
(DriveResult ? 'PUNT TD' | 'PUNT RETURN TD')
      or (DriveResult = 'PUNT' and defensive_points_scored >= 6)
      or (DriveResult = 'TD' and defensive_points_scored >= 6
          and Plays <= 4 and Yards < 15 and EndYardsToGoal = 100)

notes.text:
#|(doc)
True when the defending team ran a punt back for a touchdown, or blocked one and
returned it. Named outright by the feed on some rows (PUNT TD, PUNT RETURN TD); on the
rest it is a punt whose DEFENSE gained the points, or a short possession the feed calls
a TD that ends back on the offense's own goal line — the returner's end zone.

fields.name: is_blocked_kick_return_touchdown
fields.code:
DriveResult = 'MISSED FG TD'
      or ((DriveResult ? 'FG' | 'MISSED FG') and defensive_points_scored >= 6)

notes.text: #(doc) True when the defending team returned a blocked or missed field goal for a touchdown.
#(doc) True when the touchdown came on special teams — a kickoff return, a punt return, or a blocked kick — rather than from the offense or from a takeaway. The scoring team is this row's Defense.

fields.name: special_teams_score_type
fields.code:
pick 'Kickoff return' when is_kickoff_return_touchdown
      pick 'Punt return' when is_punt_return_touchdown
      pick 'Blocked kick return' when is_blocked_kick_return_touchdown
      else null

notes.text: #(doc) How a special-teams touchdown was scored: Kickoff return, Punt return, or Blocked kick return. Empty on every other drive.
#(doc) True when the drive ran three plays or fewer and ended in a punt, the classic three-and-out.
#(doc) True when the drive simply ran out of clock at the end of a half, a quarter, or the game.
#(doc) True when the drive gained 40 yards or more.

#|(doc)
True when the drive was a quality possession in the Eckel-rate sense: it scored a
touchdown, or it reached the opponent's 35 having gained at least ten yards. Eckel rate
proper counts a first down inside the opponent's 40, which needs play-by-play; ending
at the 35 or closer after a ten-yard gain is the drive-level stand-in.

fields.name: drive_points
fields.code:
pick EndOffenseScore - StartOffenseScore
        when EndOffenseScore - StartOffenseScore >= 0 and EndOffenseScore - StartOffenseScore <= 8
      pick 7 when DriveResult = 'TD'
      pick 3 when DriveResult = 'FG'
      else 0

notes.text:
#|(doc)
Points the offense scored on this drive, taken from the score before and after so that
extra points and two-point conversions are counted. On the 0.8% of drives where the
feed's score columns skip an intervening score and produce a value no single possession
can produce (outside 0 to 8), it falls back to the drive's result: 7 for a touchdown,
3 for a made field goal, 0 otherwise. Without that repair those 325 rows contribute 6%
of the season's points and inflate every scoring rate.

fields.name: is_named_defensive_score
fields.code:
DriveResult ? 'INT TD' | 'FUMBLE RETURN TD' | 'FUMBLE TD' | 'PUNT TD' | 'PUNT RETURN TD'
        | 'MISSED FG TD' | 'DOWNS TD' | 'END OF HALF TD' | 'END OF GAME TD' | 'SF'

notes.text: #(doc) True when the feed's own result string already says the defense scored, for example INT TD, PUNT RETURN TD, or SF.

fields.name: scoreboard_agrees_with_next_drive
fields.code:
possessions.next_offense is null
      or (possessions.next_offense != Offense
          and EndOffenseScore = possessions.next_start_defense_score
          and EndDefenseScore = possessions.next_start_offense_score)
      or (possessions.next_offense = Offense
          and EndOffenseScore = possessions.next_start_offense_score
          and EndDefenseScore = possessions.next_start_defense_score)

notes.text:
#|(doc)
True when this drive's closing scoreboard matches the next drive's opening one, with the
two teams' columns swapped if possession changed hands. Roughly 7% of consecutive drives
disagree, which is the feed's score columns lagging a possession — so this is what
separates a real defensive score from a column that simply jumped.

fields.name: defensive_points_scored
fields.code:
pick EndDefenseScore - StartDefenseScore
        when ((EndDefenseScore - StartDefenseScore >= 6 and EndDefenseScore - StartDefenseScore <= 8)
              or EndDefenseScore - StartDefenseScore = 2)
         and (is_named_defensive_score or scoreboard_agrees_with_next_drive)
      pick 2 when DriveResult = 'SF'
      pick 7 when is_named_defensive_score
      else 0

notes.text:
#|(doc)
Points the defense scored on this possession, from return touchdowns, blocked kicks
returned, and safeties. Read from the scoreboard rather than the result string, which
says how a possession ended and not who scored.

Two guardrails, both earned the hard way. A defense cannot score 3, so only a move of
6 to 8 counts as a return touchdown and only 2 as a safety. And a scoreboard move the
feed does not corroborate is not believed: of the 231 drives where the defensive column
jumps by a touchdown without the result string saying so, only 122 line up with the next
drive's opening score — the rest are the columns lagging, and counting them would invent
about a hundred defensive touchdowns.
#(doc) Kept as an alias of the points the defense scored on this possession.

fields.name: defensive_score_type
fields.code:
pick null when defensive_points_scored = 0
      pick 'Safety' when defensive_points_scored = 2
      pick 'Punt return or block' when DriveResult ? 'PUNT' | 'PUNT TD' | 'PUNT RETURN TD'
      pick 'Interception return' when DriveResult ? 'INT' | 'INT TD'
      pick 'Fumble return' when DriveResult ? 'FUMBLE' | 'FUMBLE TD' | 'FUMBLE RETURN TD'
      pick 'Blocked kick return' when DriveResult ? 'FG' | 'MISSED FG' | 'MISSED FG TD'
      else 'Return touchdown'

notes.text: #(doc) How the defense scored, when it did: Punt return or block, Interception return, Fumble return, Blocked kick return, Safety, or Return touchdown when the feed does not say. Empty when the defense did not score.

notes.text:
#|(doc)
Distance to the end zone where the OFFENSE's possession actually ended: its starting
distance less the net yards it gained, clamped into the field of play.

Not the feed's EndYardsToGoal, which on a kick or a return is where the BALL came to
rest afterwards. A punt is the clearest case: Arizona's 3-play, minus-14-yard
possession at BYU in 2026 starts on its own 25 and the feed ends it on BYU's 11, 64
yards downfield — the punt. Drawn from the feed the drive reads as a 64-yard march
instead of a three-and-out that lost ground. About a fifth of punts differ this way,
by a punt's distance (34 to 46 yards), and interceptions differ by their return.

      pick 0 when is_touchdown and not IsHomeOffense
      pick 100 - chart_end_yards_to_goal when IsHomeOffense
      else chart_end_yards_to_goal

#|(doc)
Field stripe a return touchdown started from, in absolute field coordinates.

On a KICKOFF return the feed gives the return's length in Yards (100 for BYU's
second-half return against Utah Tech in 2026), and the returning team is this row's
Defense, so the return is drawn its true length back from the goal line it reached.
A punt or blocked-kick return has no return yardage anywhere in the feed — only the
possession that preceded it — so it starts where that possession ended, which is a

fields.code:

      pick possessions.drives_left_in_game - possessions.offense_possessions_left when margin_at_drive_start > 0
      else null

fields.name: clock_ran_out
fields.code:
not is_turnover
      and not is_turnover_on_downs
      and not is_field_goal_attempt
      and EndOffenseScore = StartOffenseScore
      and EndDefenseScore = StartDefenseScore

notes.text: #(doc) True when the possession simply ran out of clock: no turnover, no points for either team, and no field goal attempt.

fields.name: is_garbage_end_of_half
fields.code:
Plays <= 2 and clock_ran_out
      and (ends_first_half or (ends_regulation and margin_at_drive_start = 0))

notes.text: #(doc) Garbage rule one: a possession of two plays or fewer that runs out the clock to end the first half, or to end regulation with the score tied, without a turnover, a score, or a field goal attempt.

fields.name: is_garbage_out_of_reach
fields.code:
StartPeriod >= 3
      and margin_at_drive_start != 0
      and 8 * losing_team_possessions_left + 1 < deficit_at_drive_start

notes.text: #(doc) Garbage rule two: a second-half possession where the game is already out of reach, because eight points times the trailing team's remaining possessions, plus one, is still less than the deficit.

fields.name: is_garbage_trailing_kneel
fields.code: Plays <= 2 and ends_game and clock_ran_out and margin_at_drive_start < -8

notes.text: #(doc) Garbage rule three: a possession of two plays or fewer by a team trailing by more than eight that runs out the clock to end the game.

fields.name: is_garbage_victory_formation
fields.code:
ends_game and clock_ran_out
      and margin_at_drive_start > 0 and margin_at_drive_start <= 8

notes.text: #(doc) Garbage rule four: the victory formation. A possession by the team ahead by eight points or fewer that runs out the clock to end the game.

fields.name: is_garbage_possession
fields.code:
(is_garbage_end_of_half
        or is_garbage_out_of_reach
        or is_garbage_trailing_kneel
        or is_garbage_victory_formation) ?? false

notes.text:
#|(doc)
True when the possession is garbage time — neither team is still playing to win it.
Covers all four of BCFtoys' rules: a kneel-down to end the first half or a tied
regulation, a second-half possession with the game already out of reach, a kneel-down
by a team trailing by more than eight, and the winning team's victory formation.
About 16% of the season's drives, and half of all fourth-quarter possessions.

fields.name: garbage_reason
fields.code:

      pick 'Trailing kneel-down' when is_garbage_trailing_kneel
      pick 'Out of reach' when is_garbage_out_of_reach
      else 'Competitive'

fields.name: is_overtime_conversion
fields.code: StartPeriod >= 5 and DriveResult = 'Uncategorized' and Plays <= 1 and Yards = 0

notes.text:
#|(doc)
True when this possession is an overtime two-point conversion attempt rather than a
drive. From the third overtime on, the rules stop giving each team a possession from
the opponent's 25 and give it a single snap from the 3 instead, alternating until one
team converts and the other does not.

The feed has no name for these. It files all nine of them under the literal result
string "Uncategorized", every one a single play that gains nothing — and that pair of
facts, inside overtime, identifies them exactly. Period alone will not do it: the
feed skips a period in Missouri-Auburn and labels an ordinary 7-play touchdown drive
as the seventh period.

#(doc) True when an overtime two-point conversion attempt was good. Read from the feed's Scoring flag, which tracks these correctly — it reproduces the 53-51 finish of the nine-period South Dakota game exactly.

fields.name: result_category
fields.code:
pick 'Two-point conversion made' when is_overtime_conversion and Scoring
      pick 'Two-point conversion failed' when is_overtime_conversion
      // ahead of both the defensive and the offensive touchdown: a kickoff
      // return is filed as the kicking team's own TD, and a punt return as
      // a plain defensive score
      pick 'Special teams touchdown' when is_special_teams_touchdown
      pick 'Defensive touchdown' when defensive_points_scored >= 6
      pick 'Safety' when defensive_points_scored = 2
      pick 'End of period' when DriveResult ? 'END OF HALF' | 'END OF GAME' | 'END OF 4TH QUARTER' | 'END OF HALF TD' | 'END OF GAME TD' | 'KICKOFF'
      pick 'Touchdown' when DriveResult = 'TD'
      pick 'Field goal' when DriveResult = 'FG'
      pick 'Punt' when DriveResult = 'PUNT'
      pick 'Missed field goal' when DriveResult = 'MISSED FG'
      pick 'Interception' when DriveResult = 'INT'
      pick 'Fumble' when DriveResult = 'FUMBLE'
      pick 'Turnover on downs' when DriveResult = 'DOWNS'
      pick 'Safety' when DriveResult = 'SF'
      else 'Uncategorized'

notes.text: #(index)

#(doc) How the drive ended, grouped into readable categories: Touchdown, Field goal, Punt, Missed field goal, Interception, Fumble, Turnover on downs, Safety, Defensive touchdown when the defense returned it for a score, End of period, Two-point conversion made and Two-point conversion failed for the alternating attempts from the third overtime on, and Uncategorized.

fields.name: result_abbreviation
fields.code:
pick '2PT' when result_category = 'Two-point conversion made'
      pick 'Miss' when result_category = 'Two-point conversion failed'
      pick 'ST TD' when result_category = 'Special teams touchdown'
      pick 'Def TD' when result_category = 'Defensive touchdown'
      // the clock running out on the game reads very differently from it
      // running out on the first half, so name them apart
      pick 'Game End' when result_category = 'End of period' and possessions.drives_left_in_game = 1
      pick 'Half' when result_category = 'End of period'
      pick 'TD' when result_category = 'Touchdown'
      pick 'FG' when result_category = 'Field goal'
      pick 'P' when result_category = 'Punt'
      pick 'FGA' when result_category = 'Missed field goal'
      pick 'Int' when result_category = 'Interception'
      pick 'Fum' when result_category = 'Fumble'
      pick 'Downs' when result_category = 'Turnover on downs'
      pick 'S' when result_category = 'Safety'
      else 'Other'

notes.text: #(doc) Short label for how the drive ended, for drive charts: TD, FG, P for punt, FGA for a missed field goal attempt, Int, Fum, Downs, S for safety, Def TD, Half when the first half ran out, Game End when the game ran out, 2PT for a converted overtime two-point attempt and Miss for one that failed, and Other.
#(doc) True when the offense scored a touchdown on this drive. False when the result string says TD but the points went to the defense.
#(doc) True when the drive ended in a made field goal by the offense. False for a kick that was blocked and returned.
#(doc) True when the drive ended in a punt.
#(doc) True when the offense turned the ball over by interception or fumble.
#(doc) True when the offense handed the ball over on downs.
#(doc) True when the drive ended in points for the offense, by touchdown or field goal.

fields.name: is_kickoff_return_touchdown
fields.code:
DriveResult = 'TD' and Plays <= 1 and Yards >= 85 and Scoring
      and EndOffenseScore - StartOffenseScore = 0

notes.text:
#|(doc)
True when this row is really a kickoff return touchdown. The feed files one under the
KICKING team as a one-play "drive" covering nearly the whole field whose own score
never moves — Utah Tech at BYU in 2026 opens the second half with "Utah Tech, 1 play,
100 yards, TD", which was BYU running the kickoff back. Read as an ordinary touchdown
it credits the wrong team, in the wrong direction. The returning team is this row's
Defense.

fields.name: is_punt_return_touchdown
fields.code:
(DriveResult ? 'PUNT TD' | 'PUNT RETURN TD')
      or (DriveResult = 'PUNT' and defensive_points_scored >= 6)
      or (DriveResult = 'TD' and defensive_points_scored >= 6
          and Plays <= 4 and Yards < 15 and EndYardsToGoal = 100)

notes.text:
#|(doc)
True when the defending team ran a punt back for a touchdown, or blocked one and
returned it. Named outright by the feed on some rows (PUNT TD, PUNT RETURN TD); on the
rest it is a punt whose DEFENSE gained the points, or a short possession the feed calls
a TD that ends back on the offense's own goal line — the returner's end zone.

fields.name: is_blocked_kick_return_touchdown
fields.code:
DriveResult = 'MISSED FG TD'
      or ((DriveResult ? 'FG' | 'MISSED FG') and defensive_points_scored >= 6)

notes.text: #(doc) True when the defending team returned a blocked or missed field goal for a touchdown.
#(doc) True when the touchdown came on special teams — a kickoff return, a punt return, or a blocked kick — rather than from the offense or from a takeaway. The scoring team is this row's Defense.

fields.name: special_teams_score_type
fields.code:
pick 'Kickoff return' when is_kickoff_return_touchdown
      pick 'Punt return' when is_punt_return_touchdown
      pick 'Blocked kick return' when is_blocked_kick_return_touchdown
      else null

notes.text: #(doc) How a special-teams touchdown was scored: Kickoff return, Punt return, or Blocked kick return. Empty on every other drive.
#(doc) True when the drive ran three plays or fewer and ended in a punt, the classic three-and-out.
#(doc) True when the drive simply ran out of clock at the end of a half, a quarter, or the game.
#(doc) True when the drive gained 40 yards or more.

#|(doc)
True when the drive was a quality possession in the Eckel-rate sense: it scored a
touchdown, or it reached the opponent's 35 having gained at least ten yards. Eckel rate
proper counts a first down inside the opponent's 40, which needs play-by-play; ending
at the 35 or closer after a ten-yard gain is the drive-level stand-in.

fields.name: drive_points
fields.code:
pick EndOffenseScore - StartOffenseScore
        when EndOffenseScore - StartOffenseScore >= 0 and EndOffenseScore - StartOffenseScore <= 8
      pick 7 when DriveResult = 'TD'
      pick 3 when DriveResult = 'FG'
      else 0

notes.text:
#|(doc)
Points the offense scored on this drive, taken from the score before and after so that
extra points and two-point conversions are counted. On the 0.8% of drives where the
feed's score columns skip an intervening score and produce a value no single possession
can produce (outside 0 to 8), it falls back to the drive's result: 7 for a touchdown,
3 for a made field goal, 0 otherwise. Without that repair those 325 rows contribute 6%
of the season's points and inflate every scoring rate.

fields.name: is_named_defensive_score
fields.code:

          and EndDefenseScore = possessions.next_start_offense_score)

notes.text:
#|(doc)
True when this drive's closing scoreboard matches the next drive's opening one, with the
two teams' columns swapped if possession changed hands. Roughly 7% of consecutive drives
disagree, which is the feed's score columns lagging a possession — so this is what
separates a real defensive score from a column that simply jumped.

fields.name: defensive_points_scored
fields.code:
pick EndDefenseScore - StartDefenseScore
        when ((EndDefenseScore - StartDefenseScore >= 6 and EndDefenseScore - StartDefenseScore <= 8)
              or EndDefenseScore - StartDefenseScore = 2)
         and (is_named_defensive_score or scoreboard_agrees_with_next_drive)
      pick 2 when DriveResult = 'SF'
      pick 7 when is_named_defensive_score
      else 0

notes.text:
#|(doc)
Points the defense scored on this possession, from return touchdowns, blocked kicks
returned, and safeties. Read from the scoreboard rather than the result string, which
says how a possession ended and not who scored.

Two guardrails, both earned the hard way. A defense cannot score 3, so only a move of
6 to 8 counts as a return touchdown and only 2 as a safety. And a scoreboard move the
feed does not corroborate is not believed: of the 231 drives where the defensive column
jumps by a touchdown without the result string saying so, only 122 line up with the next
drive's opening score — the rest are the columns lagging, and counting them would invent
about a hundred defensive touchdowns.
#(doc) Kept as an alias of the points the defense scored on this possession.

fields.name: defensive_score_type
fields.code:
pick null when defensive_points_scored = 0
      pick 'Safety' when defensive_points_scored = 2
      pick 'Punt return or block' when DriveResult ? 'PUNT' | 'PUNT TD' | 'PUNT RETURN TD'
      pick 'Interception return' when DriveResult ? 'INT' | 'INT TD'
      pick 'Fumble return' when DriveResult ? 'FUMBLE' | 'FUMBLE TD' | 'FUMBLE RETURN TD'
      pick 'Blocked kick return' when DriveResult ? 'FG' | 'MISSED FG' | 'MISSED FG TD'
      else 'Return touchdown'

notes.text:
#|(doc)
Distance to the end zone where the OFFENSE's possession actually ended: its starting
distance less the net yards it gained, clamped into the field of play.

Not the feed's EndYardsToGoal, which on a kick or a return is where the BALL came to
rest afterwards. A punt is the clearest case: Arizona's 3-play, minus-14-yard
possession at BYU in 2026 starts on its own 25 and the feed ends it on BYU's 11, 64
yards downfield — the punt. Drawn from the feed the drive reads as a 64-yard march
instead of a three-and-out that lost ground. About a fifth of punts differ this way,
by a punt's distance (34 to 46 yards), and interceptions differ by their return.

#|(doc)
Field stripe a return touchdown started from, in absolute field coordinates.

On a KICKOFF return the feed gives the return's length in Yards (100 for BYU's
second-half return against Utah Tech in 2026), and the returning team is this row's
Defense, so the return is drawn its true length back from the goal line it reached.
A punt or blocked-kick return has no return yardage anywhere in the feed — only the
possession that preceded it — so it starts where that possession ended, which is a
floor on the return, not its real length.

fields.name: losing_team_possessions_left
fields.code:
pick possessions.offense_possessions_left when margin_at_drive_start < 0
      pick possessions.drives_left_in_game - possessions.offense_possessions_left when margin_at_drive_start > 0
      else null

fields.name: clock_ran_out
fields.code:
not is_turnover
      and not is_turnover_on_downs
      and not is_field_goal_attempt
      and EndOffenseScore = StartOffenseScore
      and EndDefenseScore = StartDefenseScore

notes.text: #(doc) True when the possession simply ran out of clock: no turnover, no points for either team, and no field goal attempt.

fields.name: is_garbage_end_of_half
fields.code:
Plays <= 2 and clock_ran_out
      and (ends_first_half or (ends_regulation and margin_at_drive_start = 0))

notes.text: #(doc) Garbage rule one: a possession of two plays or fewer that runs out the clock to end the first half, or to end regulation with the score tied, without a turnover, a score, or a field goal attempt.

fields.name: is_garbage_out_of_reach
fields.code:
StartPeriod >= 3
      and margin_at_drive_start != 0
      and 8 * losing_team_possessions_left + 1 < deficit_at_drive_start

notes.text: #(doc) Garbage rule two: a second-half possession where the game is already out of reach, because eight points times the trailing team's remaining possessions, plus one, is still less than the deficit.

fields.name: is_garbage_trailing_kneel
fields.code: Plays <= 2 and ends_game and clock_ran_out and margin_at_drive_start < -8

notes.text: #(doc) Garbage rule three: a possession of two plays or fewer by a team trailing by more than eight that runs out the clock to end the game.

fields.name: is_garbage_victory_formation
fields.code:
ends_game and clock_ran_out
      and margin_at_drive_start > 0 and margin_at_drive_start <= 8

notes.text: #(doc) Garbage rule four: the victory formation. A possession by the team ahead by eight points or fewer that runs out the clock to end the game.

fields.name: is_garbage_possession
fields.code:
(is_garbage_end_of_half
        or is_garbage_out_of_reach
        or is_garbage_trailing_kneel
        or is_garbage_victory_formation) ?? false

notes.text:
#|(doc)
True when the possession is garbage time — neither team is still playing to win it.
Covers all four of BCFtoys' rules: a kneel-down to end the first half or a tied
regulation, a second-half possession with the game already out of reach, a kneel-down
by a team trailing by more than eight, and the winning team's victory formation.
About 16% of the season's drives, and half of all fourth-quarter possessions.

fields.name: garbage_reason
fields.code:
pick 'End of half kneel-down' when is_garbage_end_of_half
      pick 'Victory formation' when is_garbage_victory_formation
      pick 'Trailing kneel-down' when is_garbage_trailing_kneel
      pick 'Out of reach' when is_garbage_out_of_reach
      else 'Competitive'

#|(doc)
One row per drive (a single possession) in the 2025 and 2026 college football seasons, covering
the full Division I schedule: every FBS game and every FCS game. Each drive records who had the ball and who was
defending, when the possession started and ended on the game clock, where it started and
ended on the field, how many plays and yards it produced, how it ended (touchdown, field
goal, punt, interception, fumble, turnover on downs, end of half), and the score for both

structRef.selectStr:
WITH sides AS (
    SELECT Id AS game_id, Season AS season, "Week" AS week_number, SeasonType AS season_type,
      StartDate AS start_date, Completed AS completed, ConferenceGame AS conference_game,
      TRUE AS is_home, HomeTeam AS team, HomeConference AS conference, HomeClassification AS classification,
      AwayTeam AS opponent, AwayConference AS opponent_conference, AwayClassification AS opponent_classification,
      HomePoints AS points_for, AwayPoints AS points_against,
      HomePregameElo AS pregame_elo, HomePostgameElo AS postgame_elo, AwayPregameElo AS opponent_pregame_elo
    FROM cfb_games
    UNION ALL
    SELECT Id, Season, "Week", SeasonType,
      StartDate, Completed, ConferenceGame,
      FALSE, AwayTeam, AwayConference, AwayClassification,
      HomeTeam, HomeConference, HomeClassification,
      AwayPoints, HomePoints,
      AwayPregameElo, AwayPostgameElo, HomePregameElo
    FROM cfb_games
  )
  SELECT *,
    CAST(game_id AS VARCHAR) || '|' || team AS team_game_id,
    -- the team's most recent game that carries a postgame Elo, so a
    -- ranking can show where the rating stands now
    postgame_elo IS NOT NULL
      AND row_number() OVER (
        PARTITION BY team, season, postgame_elo IS NULL ORDER BY start_date DESC
      ) = 1 AS is_latest_rated_game
  FROM sides

fields.name: is_overtime_conversion
fields.code: StartPeriod >= 5 and DriveResult = 'Uncategorized' and Plays <= 1 and Yards = 0

notes.text:
#|(doc)
True when this possession is an overtime two-point conversion attempt rather than a
drive. From the third overtime on, the rules stop giving each team a possession from
the opponent's 25 and give it a single snap from the 3 instead, alternating until one
team converts and the other does not.

The feed has no name for these. It files all nine of them under the literal result
string "Uncategorized", every one a single play that gains nothing — and that pair of
facts, inside overtime, identifies them exactly. Period alone will not do it: the
feed skips a period in Missouri-Auburn and labels an ordinary 7-play touchdown drive
as the seventh period.

      pick 'Two-point conversion failed' when is_overtime_conversion

      pick 'Special teams touchdown' when is_special_teams_touchdown
      pick 'Defensive touchdown' when defensive_points_scored >= 6
      pick 'Safety' when defensive_points_scored = 2
      pick 'End of period' when DriveResult ? 'END OF HALF' | 'END OF GAME' | 'END OF 4TH QUARTER' | 'END OF HALF TD' | 'END OF GAME TD' | 'KICKOFF'

      pick 'Field goal' when DriveResult = 'FG'
      pick 'Punt' when DriveResult = 'PUNT'
      pick 'Missed field goal' when DriveResult = 'MISSED FG'
      pick 'Interception' when DriveResult = 'INT'
      pick 'Fumble' when DriveResult = 'FUMBLE'

notes.text:
#|(doc)

returned, and safeties. Read from the scoreboard rather than the result string, which
says how a possession ended and not who scored.

6 to 8 counts as a return touchdown and only 2 as a safety. And a scoreboard move the
feed does not corroborate is not believed: of the 231 drives where the defensive column
jumps by a touchdown without the result string saying so, only 122 line up with the next
drive's opening score — the rest are the columns lagging, and counting them would invent
about a hundred defensive touchdowns.

distance less the net yards it gained, clamped into the field of play.

regulation, a second-half possession with the game already out of reach, a kneel-down
